_README: Section copy shared by React components and scripts/prerender.mjs.
These strings previously lived inside CareerOutcomes.jsx and
PlacementPage.jsx. prerender runs in plain Node and cannot read JSX, so
the static shells for / and /placement omitted them entirely. Moving the
copy here lets both renderers read one source.
roleBlurbs is keyed by the role names in the course.roles arrays of
src/seo/routes.json. A role with no entry simply renders without a blurb.

roleBlurbs.Data Analyst: Turns raw business data into the reports and dashboards that leadership actually decides from. The most common entry point into the field.
roleBlurbs.Business Intelligence Analyst: Owns the reporting layer end to end — data models, metric definitions and the BI tooling the rest of the company relies on.
roleBlurbs.Reporting Analyst: Builds and maintains the recurring reporting that operations teams run on, and automates what used to be assembled by hand.
roleBlurbs.Data Scientist: Moves past describing what happened into predicting what will. Builds and validates models that feed real product and business decisions.
roleBlurbs.Machine Learning Engineer: Takes models out of notebooks and into production, where they have to be reliable, monitored and fast.
roleBlurbs.Applied Data Analyst: Sits between analytics and data science, using statistical methods on business problems that a dashboard cannot answer.
roleBlurbs.AI Developer: Builds applications on top of large language models — retrieval, structured prompting, evaluation and the plumbing around them.
roleBlurbs.Prompt Engineering Specialist: Designs and tests the prompts and guardrails that make an LLM behave consistently across thousands of real inputs.
roleBlurbs.AI Application Engineer: Ships user-facing AI features, owning the trade-offs between model quality, latency and cost.
roleBlurbs.Azure Data Engineer: Designs the pipelines and storage that everyone else queries. Less crowded than analytics and typically better paid.
roleBlurbs.Cloud Data Engineer: Runs data infrastructure on cloud platforms, from ingestion through transformation to serving.
roleBlurbs.Analytics Engineer: Bridges engineering and analytics — models and tests the transformed data layer that analysts build on.

placementPillars.title: Resume and LinkedIn review
placementPillars.body: A line-by-line review of your CV against the specific roles you are applying for — rewriting project descriptions so a recruiter can see the tools and the outcome in the first five seconds, which is roughly how long yours gets.

placementPillars.title: Portfolio guidance
placementPillars.body: Your course projects turned into something presentable: a clean repository, a readable summary of the problem and result, and a version of the story you can tell out loud in an interview without notes.

placementPillars.title: Mock interviews
placementPillars.body: Practice rounds covering SQL and Python problems, case-style business questions, and the project deep-dive where most candidates come unstuck. You get direct feedback on what would have ended the real interview.

placementPillars.title: Technical interview prep
placementPillars.body: Structured preparation for the rounds that actually filter candidates — window functions and joins in SQL, model evaluation reasoning in Data Science, pipeline design in Data Engineering.

placementPillars.title: Job search strategy
placementPillars.body: Where to apply, how to prioritise, and how to approach referrals. Most people lose months applying broadly through job portals; a targeted approach with a clear positioning statement works considerably better.

placementPillars.title: Mentor access during the search
placementPillars.body: Your mentor stays reachable while you are interviewing, so you can bring back real questions from real rounds instead of guessing at what went wrong.
